# @braindog/theme

**One seed colour in, a whole palette out — generated by solving for contrast, and refused if it
fails any of sixteen checks.**

Zero dependencies. Every constant has a source.

```
node src/proof.ts      # the palette, its contrast matrix, and every finding
node --test src/*.test.ts
```

---

## Why generate at all

A theme in this product is a **token document and nothing else**: it may set colour roles, a family
pairing, a spacing scale, radii and density. It may not inject CSS, target a selector, load a font,
override one block or write a hex at a call site.

That strictness is what makes sixteen block kinds look like one product. A theme that can reach past
tokens breaks all sixteen at once — and the author will never find out which one, because they will
only hear that it looks broken.

So a theme is data. And data can be generated, and generated data can be proven.

---

## Contrast-driven, not lightness-driven

Generate by lightness and validate by contrast, and you have built a loop that can fail — with a
failure mode of *"the user picked a colour and the app said no"*, repeatedly, with no path forward.

> **Generate BY contrast and the checks the generator drives become tautologies.** Only the checks it
> cannot drive — separability, ladder monotonicity — can fail. A much smaller, much more explainable
> failure surface.

```
0 NORMALISE   refuse below chroma 0.02: two identical greys can be 180° apart, and every
              derived rotation lands somewhere random
1 GROUND      dark climbs from a floor; light anchors at the TOP and descends
2 INK RAMP    bisect L for 12 : 8 : 6 : 4.5 against the WORST surface each role sits on
3 BOUNDARIES  `edge` solved for exactly 3.0; `line` decorative, and not confusable with it
4 ACCENT      the seed is the fill; the text role is solved and may sit well above 4.5
5 INTENTS     hue anchors 145 / 75 / 27, solved for text, then SEARCHED for separability
6 GAMUT MAP   CSS Color 4 §14.2.1, in JS. Never let the browser clip
7 VALIDATE    sixteen checks, both schemes, every surface
```

Every bisection runs on the **quantised, gamut-mapped** colour, because solving against the ideal and
shipping the rounded one is how a palette misses its own floor by 0.02.

---

## The measurements behind it

**Relative colour syntax is refused, and not for support.** Measured in Chrome 152:

```
oklch(0.70 C 30) painted to sRGB
  C 0.20 → rgb(255, 97, 77)
  C 0.30 → rgb(255,  0,  0)  ┐ three authored colours,
  C 0.40 → rgb(255,  0,  0)  ├ one painted colour
  C 0.50 → rgb(255,  0,  0)  ┘
```

Pure red is L ≈ 0.628, not 0.70 — so that is **clipping, not gamut mapping**. And `getComputedStyle`
hands back the authored string verbatim at every chroma, so **it cannot be detected from JavaScript.**
The generator maps in JS and emits in-gamut sRGB.

**Contrast ratio is the wrong metric for intent separability.** Under simulated dichromacy colours
collapse onto a *two-dimensional* surface — luminance plus one surviving chromatic axis — and contrast
ratio measures only luminance. It produces false failures and, worse in a ledger, false passes: two
colours thirty luminance points apart clear the floor while being "the same colour, lighter". Check F
uses **ΔE2000 on the simulated pair**, after Brettel 1997 at severity 1.0, for all three deficiencies.

**Brettel 1997, not Viénot 1999.** The single-plane simplification is valid for protan and deutan only,
and its reference implementation carries a literal warning that it is not accurate for tritanopia.

---

## Two things the generator learned by being wrong

**A contrast floor says what is legal, not what is good.** The first palette that cleared every check
had a pale-pink "overdue" in dark and a near-black one in light. Both legal; neither a colour anyone
would call overdue. The separability search now optimises against a stated preference per scheme, and
`bad` is the intent weighted hardest to hold still.

**Two intents may not share a hue, whatever the arithmetic says.** Asked to build the house theme on
the brand red as its accent, the generator succeeded: `info` came out as the mark and `bad` as a pale
tint of it, and every ΔE cleared 10 — because ΔE2000 counts lightness and two reds thirty L\* apart
are numerically far apart. They are not far apart to a reader. These intents are 12px chips compared
non-adjacently and from memory, a `warn` chip on row 3 against a `bad` chip on row 41. That is
categorical naming, and the category a person stores is the hue.

---

## Refuse, warn, or auto-correct

Three failure classes with different authors and different recoveries, so one policy would be wrong:

| Class | Policy | Argument |
|---|---|---|
| Mechanically correctable, no intent lost | **auto-correct, and show it in the install diff** | there is one right answer; refusing is pedantry |
| A floor is breached | **refuse, naming the pair and the number** | auto-correcting a contrast failure silently ships a theme the author did not make. And an auto-corrected theme is not portable, because the recipient's correction may differ — which matters most for the one artefact designed to be shared |
| Judgement, or an uncertain threshold | **warn, and let it install** | refusing on a number you have called a guess produces refusals you cannot defend |

```
theme.midnight — the pair (faint on s3) is 3.61:1. Body text needs 4.5:1.
Lighten faint to at least #8E9C96, or use it only above 24px.

theme.midnight — good and bad are delta-E 6.2 apart to a deuteranope.
Four intents need at least 10. Move one hue, or lower the chroma of the other.
```

**Two hard exceptions.** The shipped high-contrast theme is never refused and never auto-corrected: it
is the accessibility floor, so if it fails, the *validator* is wrong. And auto-correction never
crosses the WCAG line — there is no *"we nudged your `faint` up to 4.5 for you"*. That is exactly how
an ink ramp ends up with four levels where there was room for three.

---

## A finding worth keeping

The high-contrast profile holds intents at **5:1 in light, not 7:1.** Raising the floor to 7 drives
amber and red so far down the lightness axis that both bottom out against the sRGB gamut at low
chroma, and the generator measured them **9.2 apart to a protanope** — below the floor, in the one
theme that exists to serve readers who need the most help.

High contrast is a property of ink on surface and of boundaries. Forcing it onto the intent hues as
well makes the four intents *less* distinguishable, not more.

---

## Sources

Every constant is pinned, because a colour library that cannot say where its matrices came from is a
colour library nobody can check.

| | |
|---|---|
| OKLab matrices | Björn Ottosson, 2020 |
| Brettel planes | Brettel, Viénot & Mollon 1997, via libDaltonLens (public domain) |
| ΔE2000 | Sharma, Wu & Dalal 2005 |
| APCA | APCA-W3 0.1.9 — computed, stored, and **never a gate** |
| Gamut mapping | CSS Color 4 §14.2.1 |
| sRGB transfer | the exact piecewise function, not gamma 2.2 — the most-copied implementation omits this and produces visibly dark, wrong results |
